title: THE FOUR OLDS audio play — a08_diner

lines.sfx: The griddle hisses, forks knock on plates, and behind the counter a county meter ticks on the gas line.
The cook works the flat-top with his back to the room.

lines.text: (to the meter) Yeah, I see you.

lines.sfx: On the wall TV a studio crowd in matching Unity Day shirts cheers a countdown clock.
Down the counter Buck, seventy, in his feed cap, sits over a coffee with the TV going.
Earlene works the till at the end of the counter with the pot in her hand.
Buck says it down into his coffee, not loud.

lines.text: Fifty years we kept commies off the Moon. All they had to do was win a primary.

lines.sfx: The cook picks up the remote and flips it over to the ball game.
On the broadcast a ballpark public-address voice comes up over the crowd.

lines.text: Please rise for tonight's anthem, One World Rising, performed by the Children's Harmony Choir.

lines.sfx: The cook turns the TV sound down low, not off.
Buck starts humming down into his coffee, and four notes in it turns into the old anthem.
The cook's spatula picks up the time against the edge of the grill, soft, maybe not on purpose.
Earlene hums the next bar while she counts out a stranger's change.
Not a stool scrapes, and nobody says a thing.
The verse ends, and the counter goes back to forks and plates.
Down the counter Wade sits in his uniform over a plate of eggs, his hat set crown-up beside him.
His coffee cup has been empty a while now.
Earlene wipes the counter three feet from the pot and doesn't reach for it.
Wade slides two dollars under the saucer and takes up his hat.
The bell over the door rings behind him.
The bell rings again and Cricket comes in and takes the end stool, and Earlene sets a coffee down before he's square on the seat.
Buck slides the sugar caddy down the counter to him without looking up from his plate.
Cricket goes for his wallet, and Earlene is already wiping past him.
Cricket puts his cap on, and the bell rings as he goes out.
Out across the square a flag halyard taps against the courthouse pole.
The county meter ticks up another number, and the cook goes back to the grill.
